correctness.rationale: For connected simple unweighted G with oriented incidence B (one row deleted), the Euclidean cycle-space orthogonal projection is C_G=I-B^T(BB^T)^-1 B; all column-sum norms can be computed exactly as integer cofactors divided by the matrix-tree determinant. The inspected C99 verifier enumerates all labeled connected graph masks on n=2,...,6 (connected counts 1,4,38,728,26704), all 189587 missing-edge additions, and compares exact rational norms by cross-multiplication with no cycle-norm decrease. Finite exhaustive enumeration proves the finite bound if the arithmetic algorithm is sound; independently, graph_atlas_g yielded all 142 unlabeled connected isomorphism types through six vertices, and exact SymPy calculations checked all 821 non-isomorphic representatives' missing-edge insertions with no decreases. The explicit 7-vertex edge list and insertion (1,5) independently yield 313/153 to 55/27, difference 4/459. Arbitrary orientation conjugates by diagonal sign and cannot change induced l1/linfty norms. Finite assertion is genuinely exhaustive, not an extrapolation.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks corroborate only bounded cases; infinite/all-parameter assertions rest on reconstructed proof.

originality.rationale: Dilworth--Kutzarova--Ostrovskii 2023 study minimal/invariant cycle-space projections, including special graph families, but the present object is specifically the Euclidean orthogonal projector and changes its ambient edge space under insertion. Their invariant-projection constructions do not imply all-small-graph monotonicity or this sharp counterexample.
